source_question.stem: In $\triangle ABC$, an auxiliary line $l$ is drawn through vertex $A$ parallel to base $BC$. Which of the following statements provides the precise mathematical explanation for why this construction proves that $\angle A + \angle B + \angle C = 180^\circ$?

options.label: A
options.text: The line $l$ bisects angle $A$ into two equal $45^\circ$ angles.

options.label: B
options.text: The line $l$ makes side $AB$ equal in length to side $AC$.

options.label: C
options.text: The line $l$ creates alternate interior angles equal to $\angle B$ and $\angle C$ along the straight line at $A$, which sum to $180^\circ$.

options.label: D
options.text: The line $l$ forms vertically opposite angles with the base $BC$.

answer.value: The line l creates alternate interior angles equal to B and C along the straight line at A, which sum to 180

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Consider what angle relationships are created when parallel lines are intersected by transversals $AB$ and $AC$.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Examine the three adjacent angles formed at apex $A$ along the straight line $l$.

distractor_rationales.opt-A: Student erroneously assumes the triangle is right-isosceles with angle A equal to 90 degrees.
distractor_rationales.opt-B: Student confuses angle sum proof with isosceles side equality.
distractor_rationales.opt-D: Student confuses alternate interior angles across transversals with vertically opposite angles.

core1a.title: Parallel Transversals and Angle Invariance
core1a.concept: When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternate interior angles are congruent. Consecutive interior angles on the same side of the transversal sum to 180 degrees.
core1a.boundary_conditions: If lines are non-parallel, alternate interior angles are unequal and the angle-sum transfer fails.

core1b.prediction_prompt: If three adjacent angles lie along a straight line at a single vertex, what is their exact sum?
scaffold_steps: Formulate exterior angle equivalence for triangle vertices

html_representation:
In $\triangle ABC$, an auxiliary line $l$ is drawn through vertex $A$ parallel to base $BC$. Which of the following statements provides the precise mathematical explanation for why this construction proves that $\angle A + \angle B + \angle C = 180^\circ$?

Consider what angle relationships are created when parallel lines are intersected by transversals $AB$ and $AC$.

Examine the three adjacent angles formed at apex $A$ along the straight line $l$.

Review Triangle Angle Invariants
Show Complete Solution

Since line $l \parallel BC$, transversal $AB$ creates alternate interior angle $\angle 1 = \angle B$ and transversal $AC$ creates $\angle 2 = \angle C$.

Along the straight line $l$ at vertex $A$, the angles form a straight angle: $\angle 1 + \angle A + \angle 2 = 180^\circ$. Substituting gives $\angle B + \angle A + \angle C = 180^\circ$.
